english: Let $k$ be a real number and let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x+\dfrac{k}{x}$. Suppose $f$ satisfies all the conditions of Rolle's theorem on the interval $[1,4]$. If $c$ is the point of $\left(\dfrac{1}{4},25\right)$ given by Lagrange's mean value theorem for $f$ on $\left[\dfrac{1}{4},25\right]$, then the value of $c$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $k$ एक वास्तविक संख्या है तथा $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x+\dfrac{k}{x}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। मान लीजिए कि $f$ अन्तराल $[1,4]$ पर रोले प्रमेय की सभी शर्तों को सन्तुष्ट करता है। यदि $f$ के लिए अन्तराल $\left[\dfrac{1}{4},25\right]$ पर लग्रांज माध्यमान प्रमेय द्वारा प्राप्त $\left(\dfrac{1}{4},25\right)$ का बिन्दु $c$ है, तो $c$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f$ is continuous and differentiable on $[1,4]$; Rolle needs $f(1)=f(4)$: $1+k=4+\frac k4\Rightarrow k=4$ (Rolle point $c=2$).
$f'(c)=1-\dfrac{4}{c^{2}}=1-\dfrac{4}{ab}\Rightarrow c^{2}=ab=\dfrac14\cdot25\Rightarrow c=\dfrac52$ (positive root, inside the interval)
solution_full: On $[1,4]\subset(0,\infty)$, $f$ is continuous and differentiable for every $k$, so the only Rolle condition that restricts $k$ is $f(1)=f(4)$: $1+k=4+\dfrac{k}{4}\Rightarrow\dfrac{3k}{4}=3\Rightarrow k=4$. (Then $f'(x)=1-\dfrac{4}{x^{2}}=0$ at $x=2\in(1,4)$.)
So $f(x)=x+\dfrac4x$, which is continuous on $\left[\dfrac14,25\right]$ and differentiable on $\left(\dfrac14,25\right)$, so Lagrange's mean value theorem applies.
$f'(c)=1-\dfrac{4}{c^{2}}=\dfrac{9}{25}\Rightarrow c^{2}=\dfrac{25}{4}\Rightarrow c=\dfrac52$, since $c$ must lie in $\left(\dfrac14,25\right)$; $c$ is the geometric mean of the end points.
originality_note: New: Rolle's theorem fixes the parameter of f(x) = x + k/x, and the LMVT point on a second interval comes out as the geometric mean of its end points (way 5). Closest known: LMVT for 1/x giving c = sqrt(ab). Different because: the parameter is not given but recovered from Rolle's hypothesis on another interval, so both theorems are used in sequence.

concept_use.Rolle's theorem and its application: Rolle's condition f(1) = f(4) on [1,4] fixes k = 4.
concept_use.LMVT and its application: f'(c) equals the chord slope 1 - 4/(ab) on [1/4, 25], giving c = sqrt(ab) = 5/2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (positive decimal); Hindi mirrors the English maths. k is fixed by Rolle's hypothesis; the LMVT point is unique in the interval. No change.
key_step: Use f(1) = f(4) to get k, then f'(c) = 1 - 4/(ab).
justification: Two standard theorem applications in sequence, each one routine step; a routine chain at L2, like the Rolle/IVT statements of 2021-P2-Q3.
